entries.main_competence: 1.0  Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
entries.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
entries.learning_activity: (a) Describe the concept and scope of economics (meaning and origin, importance, its relationship with other subjects, basic terminologies, branches, the central economic problem and fundamental economic questions)
teaching_learning_activities: Role play: Guide students to create a list of wants and needs and use their classification rationale to relate to the concept and scope of economics

Jigsaw: Guide students to discuss meaning and origin, importance, its relationship with other subjects, basic terminologies, branches, central economic problem and fundamental economic questions in their local perspectives
The students present their findings, and the teacher relates those findings with the concept and scope of economics
entries.assessment: The concept and scope of economics is well described
resources: Bank of Tanzania (BOT) publication and reports
Tanzania Development Vision 2025 and Five-Year Development Plans
entries.references: TIE, Economics for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.main_competence: 1.0  Demonstrate mastery of basic concepts, theories and principles in Economics
entries.specific_competence: 1.1  Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and principles used in Economics
entries.learning_activity: (c) Explore the basic tenets of microeconomics (meaning, scope and goals)
teaching_learning_activities: Field trip: Students visit the nearby community and observe the prevailing economic activities, learn the way individual consumers, households, and firms make decisions, and then write the report on their observations
Discussion: Students share their experiences on the types, scopes and goals of the observed activities and present their findings
Teacher relates the students’ findings with the tenets of microeconomics
Project: Students apply tenets of micro-economics to choose a project for their club
entries.assessment: Basic tenets of microeconomics are well described
entries.references: TIE, Economics for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.learning_activity: (c) Apply production, cost and market theories to make decisions on price and output
teaching_learning_activities: Case study: Provide a case study with information on various production, cost and revenue data of the business

entries.main_competence: 2.0.  Conduct a project in Economics
entries.specific_competence: 2.1  Design and carry out a project in Economics
entries.learning_activity: (a) Design and execute a research project on an appropriate economic problem
teaching_learning_activities: Thin-ink-pair-share: Students discuss the concept of economic research
Brainstorming: Guide students to identify and discuss economic problems that affect their surrounding communities
Project: Guide students in manageable groups, guide the students to develop a mini- proposal on the selected one of the economic variables
Project: Guide students to collect data on the identified economic issue and write a report
entries.assessment: Economic research is well described, A mini-research proposal on an economic issue is well designed, Data on the identified economic issue are well collected
entries.references: TIE, Economics for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education

entries.learning_activity: (a) Design and execute a research project on an appropriate economic problem
teaching_learning_activities: Thin-ink-pair-share: Students discuss the concept of economic research
Brainstorming: Guide students to identify and discuss economic problems that affect their surrounding communities
Project: Guide students in manageable groups, guide the students to develop a mini- proposal on the selected one of the economic variables
Project: Guide students to collect data on the identified economic issue and write a report
entries.assessment: Economic research is well described, A mini-research proposal on an economic issue is well designed, Data on the identified economic issue are well collected
entries.references: TIE, Economics for Advanced Secondary Schools Form Five: Student's Book and Teacher's Guide, Tanzania Institute of Education
